independent_review.text:
# Independent shared MatCommonModule review

Subject: patch `common-module-v1.patch`, SHA-256 `7c651056f438153bf1cd6b1d992e8663de1f8d2b23cd2932086d324c70a5415e`, on `0c25c56282d805aaed351b94a9729303462bfb2a`; isolated packed artifact `38aff30dbf6c4438269bbb9bc15b9f637d2495c57847abb9532818bfb3b774cf`. The patch applied cleanly in an independent worktree, all 73 changed/deleted/new path images matched the source author's candidate, and `git diff --check` passed. All 23 deleted local stubs have identical old content: a Bidi-only NgModule.

All 21 changed family NgModules import the owned core `MatCommonModule`; all 21 family public APIs and the package root re-export the same public `@ngx-compat/material-legacy/legacy-core` symbol. The 21 family declaration files and root declaration in the packed artifact refer to the public core entrypoint; all 43 changed product TypeScript source images, including module and public API images, independently matched packed source maps. Current production legacy-core has no imports from another legacy family, so this change introduces no observed family↔core source import cycle. Existing core option module continues to use the same local core class.

At installed minimum CDK 22.1.7, `A11yModule`, `HighContrastModeDetector` and `BidiModule` are public exports and their inspected declarations are not deprecated. The owned core class imports public `A11yModule`, which in that installed peer initializes high-contrast body classes and observes forced-color changes; the add-on does not call the detector's private method. This is behavior proven for the minimum peer, not a promise about every future CDK release. The core module also exports Bidi and retains its existing owned sanity token, test-environment predicate, browser guard and doctype/theme/version checks. Untouched Material tag `df60e733...` uses a single common module, Bidi export, high-contrast initialization and three-parameter constructor; its private detector call is not copied here.

Replayed the packed six-case browser probe independently with pinned Nix Chromium 149: card, progress-bar and spinner in isolation; sanity disabled; and both modern/legacy module orders. It checked all 22 public export identities against core, injector instance, Bidi, initial forced colors and clearing, and the expected single doctype/theme warnings. The same candidate expectation against the original de6 baseline fixture failed on class identity, as intended; source trees for those three families and common core are unchanged from baseline 8baa to 0c25. Author's extracted packed ngc consumer passed, and two sequential candidate server renders ran without global window/document. These are not full browser/accessibility, hydration, concurrent SSR, error-path or M2/M3 theme-coexistence claims.

Public API exception: old add-on root/family stub classes had zero-argument constructors. The shared core class has three required parameters and requires Angular DI for normal construction. Independent TypeScript `new MatCommonModule()` control compiled against the old card entry and failed against the new declaration with TS2554, expected 3 arguments. Root's previously delegated decision accepts restoring the established three-argument historical core contract rather than inventing an outside-DI fallback. This can affect consumers of the add-on's accidental extra API; the scoped `~/cyph` search found no matching MatCommonModule/MatLegacyCommonModule usage, not proof about other consumers.

Integration blocker outside the standalone product patch: source-evidence and maintained diagnostics refer to deleted paths. In particular `scripts/upstream-bidi-evidence.mjs` requires the old module path set for the two registered Bidi subjects; `tests/bidi_module_public_probe.mjs`, `tests/upstream/bidi-peer-admission.mjs` and `tests/table_caller_roles_probe.mjs` also read deleted paths. Those existing source-bound proofs/probes cannot be treated as passing after this patch. The source author counted wider historical references, which must be preserved, and is preparing a separate reviewed evidence successor; do not recreate stubs or merely replace hashes. Other unchanged authored-use inventories likewise require their owners' review. No canonical files were modified here.

Conclusion: subject to the explicitly accepted constructor exception, the bounded shared-module behavior is supported by source and focused packed tests. It is not ready for an end-to-end audit-closure claim until the deleted-path dependencies and fresh combined packed run are handled. No security, G11, 21.x, release, or full accessibility claim.

technical_decision: Accept the historical central three-argument MatCommonModule constructor in place of accidental family/root zero-argument stubs under the user-delegated conservative TS exception. Normal Angular NgModule imports retain expected initialization; direct new of the old stub can break. Cyph scoped source search found no matching construction. Root README documents the public change.
